title: Coral Reefs
objective: After this level you can explain what coral reefs are and why they are so fragile.
summary: Corals are animals that partner with food-making algae. Reefs cover less than 1% of the ocean yet hold nearly a quarter of its species, and water that is too warm makes them bleach.

cards.headline: Earth's biggest structures made by life are built by nickel-sized animals.
cards.body: A coral polyp is soft, and most are no thicker than a nickel. But each one builds a hard limestone skeleton, and together they build coral reefs, the largest structures made by living things.

cards.headline: Animal, not plant
cards.body: Corals stay put, fixed to the seafloor like plants, but they're animals: they can't make their own food the way plants do. So they take in lodgers. Tiny algae called zooxanthellae live inside the coral's tissue. The coral gives them a home, and the algae use sunlight to make food and share it. They're the coral's main food source. Rent, paid in lunch.

cards.fact: Coral reefs cover less than 1% of the ocean, yet nearly a quarter of all ocean species live there.
cards.context: Reef-building corals grow in clear, warm, moving water in tropical and subtropical seas, where sunlight can reach their algae. Sound familiar? Level 42's rainforests pull the same trick on land: a small slice of Earth holding more than half of its plant and animal species.

cards.headline: Why a coral turns white
cards.body: When the water gets too warm, stressed corals expel the algae living in their tissues and turn completely white. That's coral bleaching. Those algae were the coral's main food and its color, so a bleached coral isn't dead yet, but it's starving. If the stress eases, it can recover. If the heat goes on, it eventually dies.

mascot.line: Bleached doesn't mean dead. That's the detail people most often get wrong.
